items.prompt: Rice, bread and noodles are rich in which food group?

options.why: Proteins come from foods like fish, eggs and tempeh.
Vitamins come mostly from fruit and vegetables.
Fats come from foods like oil and butter.

hints: These foods give you lots of energy.
Think of the group that gives energy for running and playing.
This group's name is a long word that starts with c.
items.explanation: Rice, bread and noodles are rich in carbohydrates. Carbohydrates give your body energy.

items.prompt: Sort the foods into food groups.
hints: Think about what each food mostly gives your body.
Starchy foods give energy. Foods for growing often come from animals or beans.
Put the fruit and vegetables together first.
items.explanation: Rice, bread and potatoes are carbohydrates. Eggs, tempeh and fish are proteins, and spinach, oranges and papaya give vitamins and minerals.

items.prompt: Match each food group to its main job.
pairs: help the body grow and repair
store energy and keep the body warm
helps food move through the gut
hints: Each food group does a different job.
Think about which foods help you grow taller and heal cuts.
Start with carbohydrates. What do rice and bread give you?
items.explanation: Carbohydrates give energy and proteins help you grow and repair. Fats store energy, vitamins and minerals keep you healthy, and fibre helps food move through your gut.

items.prompt: Which food is a good source of protein?

options.why: Rice is mostly carbohydrate, for energy.
Cucumber is mostly water, with a few vitamins.
Sugar is a carbohydrate that gives quick energy.

hints: Protein often comes from animals, beans or soya.
Which food is made from soya beans?
items.explanation: Tempeh is made from soya beans and has lots of protein. Protein helps your body grow and repair itself.

items.prompt: Milk helps build strong bones and teeth. Which mineral in milk helps most?

options.why: Iron helps your blood carry oxygen.
Sugar gives energy. It does not build bones.
Vitamin C helps you heal and fight illness. It is not a mineral.

hints: Bones and teeth are hard and white.
This mineral is also found in cheese and yoghurt.
Its name starts with the letter c.
items.explanation: Milk contains calcium. Calcium helps build strong bones and teeth.

items.prompt: Choose 2 foods that are high in fibre.

options.why: Butter is mostly fat. It has no fibre.
Eggs have lots of protein but no fibre.
Milk has calcium and protein but no fibre.

hints: Cross out the foods that come from animals.
Count the foods that are left.
items.explanation: Fibre comes from plant foods. Brown rice and beans have lots of fibre, which helps food move through your gut.

items.prompt: Dimas eats rice, fried chicken and fried tempeh for lunch. Which food group is missing?

options.text: vitamins and minerals from fruit or vegetables

options.why: The rice gives carbohydrates.
The chicken and tempeh give lots of protein.
Fried foods are cooked in oil, which is fat.

hints: Name the food group of each food on the plate.
Rice, chicken and tempeh are all there. What is not?
Look for something green or colourful that is missing.
items.explanation: Dimas has carbohydrates, proteins and some fat. He has no fruit or vegetables, so his meal is missing vitamins, minerals and fibre.

items.prompt: Which lunch box has the best mix of food groups?

options.why: These are all carbohydrates. There is no protein or vegetables.

options.text: rice, egg, spinach and a banana

options.why: These are mostly protein and fat. There is no fruit or vegetable.
These are mostly sugar. They are fine sometimes, but not as a whole meal.

hints: A good meal has foods from different groups.
Count how many food groups each lunch box has.
Look for a box with energy food, protein and a vegetable or fruit.
items.explanation: Rice gives energy, egg gives protein, and spinach and banana give vitamins, minerals and fibre. This mix of groups makes a balanced meal.

items.prompt: Long ago, sailors ate only dry bread and salted meat for months. Many became ill. Which food would have helped most?

options.why: Salted meat gives protein. The sailors were missing vitamins.
Bread gives energy. It does not have the vitamin they needed.
Sea water is too salty to drink and has no vitamins.

hints: Think about which food group was missing.
Bread and meat give energy and protein.
items.explanation: The sailors were missing vitamin C, which comes from fresh fruit and vegetables. Oranges and limes are full of vitamin C.

items.prompt: Your body needs ___ to grow and to repair cuts. Fish, eggs and beans have lots of it.
hints: Think of the food group for growing.
Tempeh and tofu are rich in it too.
items.explanation: Protein helps your body grow and repair itself. Fish, eggs, beans, tempeh and tofu are good sources.

items.prompt: A drink label says it has 30 g of sugar. One teaspoon of sugar is about 5 g. About how many teaspoons is that?
hints: Count in fives until you reach 30.
items.explanation: 30 g shared into 5 g teaspoons makes 6 teaspoons. That is a lot of sugar for one drink, so water is a better everyday choice.

items.prompt: Two meals give the same amount of energy. Meal X: rice, fish and spinach. Meal Y: noodles, bread and potato. Which is better for a growing child?

options.text: Meal Y, because it has more carbohydrates
options.why: Meal Y has lots of carbohydrates but no protein or vegetables.

options.text: Both are the same, because the energy is the same
options.why: Energy is only one need. Growing bodies also need protein and vitamins.

options.text: Meal Y, because it has three foods
options.why: Meal X also has three foods, and they come from more groups.

options.text: Meal X, because it has foods from more food groups

hints: Energy is not the only thing a body needs.
Sort each meal's foods into food groups.
Which meal has protein and a vegetable?
items.explanation: Meal Y is all carbohydrates. Meal X has carbohydrate, protein from fish, and vitamins and minerals from spinach, so it is better balanced.
